title: Volcan: hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff

beats.narration_text: An autonomous coding agent just wrote this patch. A sighted reviewer scans it in seconds. A screen reader reads it one plus sign, one minus sign and one hunk header at a time, so the single line that flips an authorization check sounds exactly like everything around it.
beats.visual_action: Screen recording of a screen reader reading the raw unified diff in the patch box of the companion page at http://127.0.0.1:8000/, opened with Alt and 2, with the reader's own speech as the only audio.

beats.narration_text: This is Volcan, running on this machine. Before anything plays, the stage already shows the server's real answer for this patch, silently: the earcon's waveform with its falling pitch, the finding in words, and the Braille cells. One button plays it. The earcon comes first, so the verdict arrives before the sentence. This patch touches security, so the cue falls; a benign one rises. Then the spoken digest, which opens with the finding itself: an authorization comparison was inverted. The engine label and the round trip are read off the response, measured in this browser.
beats.visual_action: Open on the first paint: the stage already shows the silent preview, the waveform in its not yet heard colour with the Falling contour, the finding sentence, the eight-dot Braille cells and the line Server's first sentence, not played yet. Press Alt and 1 to focus Hear this code review, then Enter. Hold on the playhead crossing the waveform, the words lighting as the browser speaks them, finding first, and the three meters filling with the engine name, the measured round trip and the change size.

beats.narration_text: The track question is whether the protocol is real. Volcan's Model Context Protocol server is written by hand to revision 2025-11-25 over Streamable HTTP, with no SDK. This button performs a real initialize and a real tools list call against the MCP endpoint, then prints the negotiated version, the session identifier taken from the response header, and the JSON Schema of all twelve tools. The conformance script runs the same handshake from a terminal.
beats.visual_action: In Evidence, tab Server and MCP, click Run a real MCP handshake, hold on the four facts and one expanded tool schema, then cut to a terminal running python scripts/mcp_conformance.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp and its pass lines.

beats.narration_text: A high-consequence command is staged behind a single-use grant, bound by HMAC SHA-256 to the command's own payload hash and to a lease. The agent that proposed the action cannot release it. A human presents the grant, and the planner answers: allowlisted, would run git diff HEAD, executed is false. Nothing ran. That holds for the whole product. No file under src imports subprocess or any process spawn, and a test walks every module's syntax tree on each run to keep it that way.
beats.visual_action: In Evidence, select the Governed actions tab and click Stage an action, hold on the lease countdown, click Approve with the grant, hold on the line that reads Dry run only, nothing was executed, and on the audit row reading released to you, nothing run. Cut to a terminal running python -m pytest tests/unit/test_no_execution_in_source_tree.py -q.

beats.narration_text: Everything shown here is checkable in one command. Five hundred and forty-three automated tests. Twenty-two of twenty-two protocol conformance checks. And a readiness script that is allowed to fail, and does: no video has been rendered yet, and the deployed endpoint is an older commit than this one. There is no Alexa skill in this repository and no Bedrock model was called from this machine. The page says both on screen. Volcan is for the developer who reviews code by ear and by touch.
beats.visual_action: Terminal running python -m pytest tests/ -q, then python ci/readiness.py scrolled to its red gates, then back to the companion page: in Evidence, tab Server and MCP, the connection strip stating the resolved model path the server reported, which on the development machine reads unavailable_sdk_not_installed. Close on the page heading.
